c.tagline: Flores gateway to Komodo dragons, pink beaches and world-class diving.

taxi.fareNote: There are no metered street taxis; agree a price before the ride or use a hotel car. Grab coverage is limited, so ojek motorbike taxis and negotiated van hires are the norm.

emergency.note: 112 is the general nationwide emergency line reachable from mobiles; 110 reaches police and 118/119 the ambulance service. Medical facilities are basic — serious cases are evacuated to Bali.

avoid.reason: Vet Komodo boat operators' safety records before booking, and watch belongings in waterfront bars where occasional petty theft occurs.

hood_desc: The buzzing heart of Labuan Bajo along Jalan Soekarno-Hatta and the harbour, where boats depart for Komodo, dive shops line the street and the Kampung Ujung night market grills fresh seafood; the most convenient, walkable base for first-timers.

A quieter stretch of beach a few kilometres north of town with dive resorts, guesthouses and calm swimming; suits divers and travellers wanting the water at their doorstep away from the harbour bustle.
A public beach just south of the centre known for sunsets, beach clubs and nearby upscale resorts such as Ayana; a relaxed, scenic base within easy reach of town.
An inland village around the Batu Cermin (Mirror Cave) with budget homestays and a local feel, a short ride from the harbour; suits budget travellers wanting a quieter, authentic stay.
The hillside above the harbour around Puncak Waringin, dotted with boutique hotels and villas that trade beach access for sweeping sunset views over the bay and islands; best for a scenic splurge.

water.note: Drink bottled or refill-station filtered water only.

transit.hours: There is no scheduled public-transport timetable; ojek motorbike taxis and rented scooters run through the day, while cars can be booked at any hour by phone or through hotels.
transit.note: Labuan Bajo has no formal city bus or rail network; the compact town is walkable, and travellers get around by ojek (motorbike taxi), rented scooter, hotel car or the limited Grab app. Nearly all sightseeing is by boat into Komodo National Park.
transit.pay: Ride fares are paid in cash and usually negotiated before you set off; scooter rentals run around Rp 75,000-100,000 (~$5-7) a day, and boat trips are booked and paid through tour operators.

bus: Trans-Flores buses and shared minibuses (travel) east to Ruteng, Bajawa, Ende and Maumere
ferry: Labuan Bajo port: ASDP car ferry west to Sape (Sumbawa), Pelni inter-island liners, and daily tour boats and liveaboards to Komodo National Park

transit.m: Airport taxi or hotel shuttle to the town centre (~10 min)
Ojek (motorbike taxi) to the harbour (~10 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not obligatory but increasingly expected in tourism; rounding up, or leaving 5-10% for guides, boat crews and drivers, is much appreciated.

food.name: Ikan bakar
food.desc: Reef fish caught that morning, split, rubbed with chilli-garlic paste and grilled over coconut husk, served with rice and sambal.

places.name: Kampung Ujung night market
places.note: Rows of grill stalls where you pick your fish from ice and it is cooked in front of you.

places.name: Warung Mama
places.note: Simple local warung on the main street known for Flores-style grilled fish and sambal.

places.name: Pasar Baru Labuan Bajo
places.note: Town market where the same catch is sold and cooked by stallholders at local prices.

food.name: Udang dan lobster bakar
food.desc: Prawns, squid and small lobster from the Flores Sea grilled with butter, lime and chilli; the night-market splurge.

places.name: Kampung Ujung night market
places.note: Best value seafood in town; agree the price per kilo before ordering.

places.name: Waterfront seafood grills on Jalan Soekarno Hatta
places.note: Harbour-side kitchens grilling the day's shellfish with sunset views.

places.name: Pasar Baru Labuan Bajo
places.note: Buy live shellfish in the morning and have a warung cook it.

food.name: Se'i sapi
food.desc: East Nusa Tenggara smoked beef, cured over kosambi wood until pink and tender, sliced thin and served with chilli-and-lime sambal luat.

places.name: Warung Mama
places.note: Local warung serving the NTT smoked beef with rice and sambal luat.

places.name: Kampung Ujung night market

food.name: Jagung bose
food.desc: Hulled corn slow-simmered with red beans and coconut milk into a thick savoury porridge, the traditional staple of the region.

places.name: Warung Mama

places.name: Pasar Baru Labuan Bajo

places.name: Warungs on Jalan Yohanes Sehadun
places.note: Family kitchens where corn and beans still replace rice.

food.name: Ikan kuah asam
food.desc: Clear sour fish soup sharpened with belimbing wuluh, tomato, turmeric and basil, eaten as a light counterpoint to grilled fish.

places.name: Warung Mama
places.note: Home-style sour fish broth cooked to order.

places.name: Kampung Ujung night market

places.name: Pasar Baru Labuan Bajo
places.note: Market warungs serve it as breakfast with rice.

food.name: Nasi kolo
food.desc: Manggarai rice cooked inside a bamboo tube over open fire, faintly smoky, traditionally eaten at village ceremonies with chicken.

places.note: Manggarai dishes including bamboo-cooked rice when available.

places.name: Melo village cultural kitchens

places.name: Pasar Baru Labuan Bajo

food.name: Kopi Flores Manggarai
food.desc: Arabica grown on the volcanic slopes of Manggarai and Bajawa, brewed strong and black; the region's proudest export.

landmarks: Komodo Island (Komodo National Park)
The legendary UNESCO island where rangers lead treks among wild Komodo dragons, the planet's largest lizards, in savanna hills ringed by coral seas.
Padar Island
An iconic ridge-top viewpoint overlooking three crescent bays of pink, white and black sand, the single most photographed panorama in Komodo National Park.
Pink Beach (Pantai Merah)
A blush-colored strand tinted by crushed red coral, where snorkelers drift over vibrant reef gardens right off the shoreline.
Rinca Island
Komodo's quieter sister island, whose dry hills and ranger-guided boardwalk trails offer some of the most reliable dragon sightings in the park.
Manta Point
A current-swept channel in the national park where snorkelers and divers glide alongside squadrons of reef manta rays year-round.
Batu Cermin Cave (Mirror Rock Cave)
A limestone cave outside town where midday sun beams bounce off crystalline walls, illuminating fossilized coral embedded in the rock.
Cunca Wulang Waterfall
A jungle canyon an hour inland where waterfalls pour into emerald swimming holes carved through the gorge, nicknamed Flores's mini Grand Canyon.
Rangko Cave
A hidden sea cave near Labuan Bajo whose turquoise saltwater pool glows under shafts of sunlight, reached by boat and a short walk.
Kelor Island
A tiny cone-shaped isle close to the harbor whose short, steep climb rewards with postcard views and whose beach offers superb snorkeling.
Kampung Ujung Night Fish Market
Labuan Bajo's waterfront evening market, where the day's catch is grilled to order at plastic tables overlooking the boat-filled harbor.

train.note: There are no railways anywhere on Flores, so no passenger trains serve Labuan Bajo.

bus.note: No international coaches. Buses and shared minibuses (travel/bemo) run the long Trans-Flores highway east to Ruteng, Bajawa, Ende and Maumere; most visitors instead hire a car and driver for these multi-day overland trips.

ferry.note: No international ferries. Labuan Bajo's port is a busy domestic hub: ASDP car ferries cross west to Sape on Sumbawa, Pelni liners call on their inter-island routes, and countless tour boats and liveaboards depart daily for Komodo National Park, Rinca and the dive sites.

half.name: Melo Village
half.blurb: A Manggarai hilltop village a short drive from Labuan Bajo where visitors watch the caci whip-dance and see traditional round houses.

half.name: Cunca Rami Waterfall
half.blurb: A tiered jungle waterfall southeast of Labuan Bajo reached by a short trek, with a swimming pool at its base separate from Cunca Wulang.
